evidence: scripts/helpers/msi.ps1 falls back to version 1.0.0 when -Version is omitted and no assembly/file version can be resolved.
tasks.impact: The canonical MSI build flow produces a static 1.0.0 installer unless a version is supplied manually, which weakens artifact traceability and makes default upgrade validation less representative.
tasks.recommended_action: Introduce a repository-owned installer version source and consume it from scripts\packaging\msi-build.ps1 and CI when -Version is not provided.

evidence: Running .\scripts\pack.ps1 -Configuration Release -SkipRestore -SkipBuild produced artifacts\packages\Release\net8.0-windows\Viewer\NtfsAudit.App.exe and artifacts\packages\Release\net8.0-windows\Viewer\NtfsAudit.App.dll alongside NtfsAudit.Viewer.exe.
src/NtfsAudit.Viewer/App.xaml.cs directly uses NtfsAudit.App.MainWindow and NtfsAudit.App.ViewModels.MainViewModel.
tasks.impact: The read-only viewer package currently ships the main application executable, which blurs the component boundary and increases the chance of launching the wrong entrypoint from the viewer distribution.
tasks.recommended_action: Split the shared UI/view-model surface needed by NtfsAudit.Viewer into a dedicated library or otherwise remove the direct executable project dependency before repackaging the viewer.

evidence: Running .\scripts\pack.ps1 -Configuration Release -SkipRestore -SkipBuild produced runtime payloads under artifacts\packages\Release\net8.0-windows\App\runtimes, Viewer\runtimes, and Service\runtimes that include linux, osx, maccatalyst, and browser-wasm assets.
The repository is Windows-first and all application projects target windows-specific frameworks.
tasks.impact: Default package outputs and downstream MSI inputs include non-Windows runtime assets, inflating package size and review surface for Windows-only distributions.
tasks.recommended_action: Evaluate making RID-specific Windows packaging the default distribution path or prune non-Windows transitive runtime assets from the framework-dependent packaging outputs.
